mainEntity.name: Who is responsible when an AI workflow makes a bad business decision?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Use a workflow only when it has a clear owner, defined review standard, and a way to pause or correct it. AI can draft recommendations, but the owner remains responsible for deciding whether the result is accurate, appropriate, and useful.

## Context
Run My AI Business repeatedly emphasizes human-directed automation, approval before consequential actions, source verification, and owner control over decisions, spending, and publication.

## Key factors
- Who approves the output
- What quality standard applies
- What happens when confidence is low
- How corrections are recorded

## Practical guidance
Name an owner for every workflow and set a review schedule. Include a pause instruction, an escalation contact, and a record of changes so the process does not continue using outdated assumptions.

This is especially important when several assistants coordinate around one business project.
acceptedAnswer.description: The business owner remains responsible for decisions and consequential actions. Assign a named workflow owner, define quality standards, require approval where risk is meaningful, log exceptions, and provide a way to pause the workflow when information is uncertain or outdated.
